en: The Brief Sūtra on the Analysis of Karmic Retribution,
compiled by the Bodhisattva Mahāśūra and translated by the Tripitaka Master Saṃghavarman of India during the Song Dynasty.
To the Most Victorious and Unsurpassed Honored One, who is fully endowed with knowledge and vision, I prostrate;
likewise to the Dharma and the Saṅgha of the True Sages.
I now compile this Abhidhamma, spoken by one fully endowed with knowledge and vision.
The arising of the five destinies is due to pure and impure karma.
For the sake of all the worlds, he reveals the meaning of the sūtras;
according to the reach of his wisdom, he analyzes the retribution of karmic actions.
The Buddha, having attained self-awakening through the Dharma, was entreated by all the devas;
he then proceeded to Vārāṇasī to expound the meaning of the True Truths:
namely, suffering and the cause of suffering, and the ultimate cessation of the accumulation of suffering.
Fully endowed with the Eightfold Path, it is the pure way to end suffering.
The Unsurpassed Honored One among men has taught that the retribution for the karma of suffering arises from this successive production of afflictions and all manner of karmic deeds.
The various characteristics of the afflictions and the immeasurable activities of karma are briefly distinguished here in sequence, in accordance with the teachings of the Great Sage.
As revealed in the sūtras, this does not contradict the characteristics of all phenomena.
The wise should uphold this definitive meaning of reality:
it is not created by Īśvara; its fruition is not without cause;
nor does it arise from intrinsic nature (svabhāva), nor is it born from time.
Iśvara is not the cause, nor are self-nature or time;
because effects possess degrees of excellence and inferiority, one should know that these are not the causes.
Ignorance gives rise to afflictions, and from these, all karmas arise.
Karma causes the opening of various realms; now I shall explain their distinctions.
Having committed various unwholesome karmas, beings enter the evil destinies according to their karma.
To those sinful beings, King Yama speaks with compassion:
The sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death, and the constraints of royal law—
seeing those messengers of the gods, why do you not give rise to supreme awakening?
Through wise giving and pure precepts, one can discipline body, speech, and mind.
For what do you seek, that you do not make the supreme vow?
Unfortunate as it is to encounter evil friends and hear only matters contrary to the Dharma,
which increase my greed, anger, and delusion— by what means can pure karma be generated?
"You never cultivated goodness, But committed only various evil deeds;
Unaware that the retribution for your sins had arrived, You have now come to enter hell.
At that time, the various hell-wardens Immediately seize the sinful beings.
Driven toward the gates of hell, one’s hair stands on end with terror.
The Reviving, the Black String, the Crushing, and the Two Screaming Hells,
The Avīci Great Hell, the Heating, and the Great Heating— these are the eight great hells.
The Muddy Sea and the Pit of Excrement, The Forest of Sword-Leaved Trees,
the Path of Knives, and the Tree with Sword Branches, The River of Ashes and the Iron Cauldron Hell—
Those who have committed various evil deeds Are born within these hells.
I shall now explain that karma and the characteristics of its various bitter retributions:
being revived after death and reborn again, one undergoes this for billions of kalpas because of harboring resentment and hatred, and because of mutual injury.
Deceiving others by unrighteous means, using double-tongued speech to alienate friends,
slandering, and speaking falsehoods— upon death, one falls into the Black Rope Hell.
Those who slaughter or capture animals and commit other acts of killing— upon death, they enter the Hell of Collapsing Mountains.
Grinded and crushed by all manner of mountains, their bodies shattered and their blood and marrow flowing;
ruling without compassion or pity, they employ severe laws for many reasons,
establishing numerous expedients to inflict various forms of torture and agony.
They also enter the Saṃghāta Hell, suffering retribution according to their karma.
They revolve upon crumbling mountain peaks and are ground and pounded by iron stones;
following greed, anger, delusion, and fear, they adjudicate lawsuits by perverting the upright with the crooked.
They shall likewise enter the Saṃghāta Hell, where iron wheels sever their bodies.
Relying on their own powerful might, they were treacherous and violent, bullying the solitary and the weak;
they shall likewise enter the Saṃghāta Hell, where black elephants come vying with one another to trample them.
Oppressing many people, causing them to cry out in lamentation,
one dies and falls into the Raurava Hell, where the entire body is constantly ablaze.
Deceiving others with false scales and measures, one is evil in heart though sweet in speech.
If one’s words and deeds lack sincerity, one enters the Hell of Great Screaming.
Alas, the Hell of Great Screaming! Those who see it have their hair stand on end;
therein one undergoes extreme suffering because of failing to return what was entrusted to one.
To call what is not the Dharma "the Dharma," and to see the Dharma as "not the Dharma";
to hold false views that deny cause and effect, and to treat the noble sages with contempt and slander—
such persons as these shall, upon death, enter the Avīci Hell.
If one offends or causes distress to virtuous parents, to śramaṇas, or to brāhmaṇas,
one will enter the Saṃjīva (Reviving) Hell after death.
[The same applies to] offending virtuous parents, śramaṇas, or brāhmaṇas.
With an evil mind, one inflicts suffering; upon death, one enters the Great Heat Hell.
Having left the household life to cultivate pure conduct, yet violating the rules of discipline and mutual disparagement, upon death, one enters the Hot Earth Hell.
Transgressing prohibitions and abandoning right livelihood, one earns a defiled existence through crookedness and deceit;
upon death, one enters the Hot Feces Pond, where venomous insects pierce the very marrow of the bones.
Hunting and burning forests and marshes, one scorches and harms the sentient beings of the land.
Upon death, they enter the Hell of Fire-Swords, where their limbs and joints are burned, flayed, and severed.
Having lured and seized various sentient beings under the guise of kinship, they take their lives;
then crows, ravens, and packs of starving dogs vied with one another to devour their flesh.
Destroying the bridge of the True Dharma, they lead people toward unrighteous conduct;
at death, they traverse the path of sharp blades, their feet severed and their flesh and bones cut away.
With bodies long as a centipede, they appear in the likeness of beautiful women.
Enveloped by [worms] that gnaw at their marrow and brain— this is due to their practice of sexual misconduct.
Having touched the bodies of other men's wives with deep attachment,
they are driven up the sword-leaf trees, where their bodies are pierced as they move back and forth.
Employing various skillful means, they kill all kinds of aquatic creatures;
upon death, they enter the River of Boiling Ashes, their entire bodies completely mangled and putrefied.
They swallow glowing iron balls, and molten copper is poured into their mouths.
Iron nails are driven into their bodies because they stole the wealth of others.
Through the intensification of the ten unwholesome actions, when their spirits depart, they enter hell;
next, by secondary offenses, they fall among the animals; the remainder enter the realm of hungry ghosts.
Harboring hatred and committing unwholesome deeds, with a mind that constantly delights in evil dharmas,
one who rejoices at the suffering of others will become a henchman of Yama after death.
Having thus explained the various types of karmic actions, those that are most grave lead to rebirth in hell.
Now I shall explain the karmic retribution of animals and hungry ghosts.
Through the three faults of body and the four of speech, as well as the three unwholesome states of mind—
if these actions are not intensified— one falls into the realm of animals at death.
Those with many desires are born as geese, pigeons, peacocks, and mandarin ducks;
those born from the karma of folly become maggots, ants, moths, and the like.
Those lacking wisdom who delight in beating and binding are reborn among elephants and horses as their retribution.
Or again, they become oxen and sheep, or deer and various wild beasts;
through anger and hatred they become vipers and snakes, or species of bees, scorpions, and venomous insects;
through arrogance and self-conceit, they harbor malice in secret with evil intent.
As retribution for past lives, one may become a *kharoṣṭra* with eight legs, or a tiger or a lion;
as retribution for arrogance and harshness, one becomes a pig, a dog, a donkey, a fox, or a wolf.
One who is quick-tempered, envious, full of hatred, and whose mind is frivolous and unstable—[will suffer such fates].
After death, one falls among the monkeys;
being insincere and given to excessive speech, one receives the retribution of karma and later takes the body of a crow.
Through divisive speech one severs close friends; later, one receives the body of a cat or a wildcat, or perhaps the body of a bear or a grizzly.
Being quick-tempered and full of anger, one does not rely upon right mindfulness.
Later, he became a dragon of great power;
with a haughty mind that looked down upon others, through such karmic actions,
he was born as a powerful garuḍa.
Those who consume various delicacies and fine foods may fall among the *pūtana* ghosts,
eating excrement and corpses;
those who suffer from disease, poverty, or begging will later become *piśāca* ghosts.
Constantly consuming various fetuses and webs,
stingy, parsimonious, and full of greedy desires, one becomes a lowly hungry ghost after death,
with an extremely dark and emaciated body.
Some give and yet destroy themselves; after death they fall among the vomit-eating spirits, feeding only on pus, mucus, and spittle.
They disparage others' practice of giving, being stingy and cherishing what is bitter and coarse.
Delighting in the practice of base and defiled deeds, dwelling hidden beneath the flow of a drain,
and constantly eating all manner of impurities;
possessing wealth yet not using it, one would rather discard it than practice giving.
Upon death, they fall among the wrathful hungry ghosts;
having harmed others and seized their wealth, they fall as hungry ghosts due to their remaining offenses,
constantly consuming the vital essence of humans.
Delighting in exposing the private faults of others, Stubborn and difficult to subdue,
one is reborn as a fire-mouthed hungry ghost.
Accumulating wealth while constantly fearing its depletion, Lacking compassion and being stubborn by nature—
Later, one becomes a fire-eating insect-demon, constantly devouring moths and ants,
with one’s entire body ablaze.
One who suppresses the giving of others and, though possessing wealth, refuses to relinquish it, will be reborn as a giant-bodied demon.
With a belly as vast as a mountain yet a throat like a needle,
they accumulate [wealth] for their descendants; by reason of such karmic conditions,
they are later reborn as hungry ghosts of the "Light" class.
If descendants cultivate merit on one's behalf, they may thereby obtain food through faith. Yet,
by forcibly taking the wealth of others to give as alms, one dies to become a kumbhāṇḍa,
whose eating and drinking are always according to his own will.
By giving meat as an act of charity, one becomes a rākṣasa for remaining karmic offenses,
yet constantly obtains various fine foods.
By constantly practicing the cultivation of generosity, one naturally adorns one's body with fragrant flowers.
Those who delight in various performances and music will later become gandharvas,
the celestial musicians who attend to the gods.
Those who are prone to anger and fond of double-tongued speech will later become piśācas.
His body was exceedingly ugly, with disheveled hair and bloodshot eyes,
sharp claws and long fangs;
yet he practiced generosity extensively, though his nature was fond of pleasure and his mind was flighty and restless.
Born as the ghost Buhu,
he delighted in practicing generosity; though fond of wine and enjoying song and dance,
he was later reborn as an earth deity.
One who gives alms to those who are kind and virtuous, yet is by nature very stingy,
will be reborn as a sky-wandering deity.
By practicing such generosity, one is reborn as a deity of the void.
It is always accompanied by palaces.
I have already briefly distinguished the realms of animals and hungry ghosts;
now I shall explain in due order the fruits of the paths of humans and devas.
Those born thereafter in the happy realms receive their retribution according to their karma;
this I shall now explain as it truly is.
For those who seek long life, the non-harming of living beings is the foundation.
The wise should know this:
those who delight in cultivating all meritorious qualities will be firm and unshakable,
and their rebirths shall be free from all hardships.
By not beating or binding others, through this karma of non-affliction,
one will never be ill in whatever birth one takes.
By not stealing the wealth of others, one will never suffer from lack or deprivation in whatever birth one takes.
Seeking much yet obtaining little,
and furthermore seizing the property of others, one will always obtain wealth in whatever life one is born,
but as soon as it is gained, it is lost again.
At times practicing even slight acts of giving, one obtains wealth and profit through skillful means,
and what is gained is never lost;
furthermore, by extensively practicing giving, one is immediately born into great wealth.
One shall acquire wealth that is never lost;
wherever one is born, one shall encounter the True Dharma; all who see one shall love and delight in them;
and one’s fame shall spread far and wide.
Easy to satisfy, knowing contentment; serene and at ease, free from sorrow and affliction;
upright and honest, practicing right conduct.
Cultivating meritorious deeds with a faithful heart, wherever one may be born, [one shall find happiness].
One will always inherit the father’s remaining wealth;
possess long life, a fine complexion, and strength; be eloquent, wise, and rich in treasures;
and remain free from illness with a peaceful and happy mind.
The divine form is sublime and honored, replete with all the marks of a great man;
those who behold it cannot fail to rejoice, for his body is ever at peace and his mind is constantly filled with joy.
By giving a house, one obtains a residence, a palace of supreme magnificence and beauty,
with treasure-troves all filled to overflowing, and every requisite provided according to one's desire.
If one gives wells, bathing pools, and pure water or refreshing drinks, [one gains these rewards].
In every birth they shall never suffer from thirst or want, and their desires shall always be fulfilled as they wish.

By providing bridges and boats for those who have not yet crossed, and by giving sandals to those who walk barefoot, they shall always obtain elephants, horses, and carriages; such a person is a god among men.
If one gives gardens and groves as a gift, one will constantly obtain superior and wondrous fruits:
they will become a refuge for all, their minds peaceful and free from the heat of affliction;
they will be beloved by all people, and their retinue will be fully complete.
If a person gives medicine as an offering, they will be born in the future free from illness,
enjoying long life and constant peace and happiness, endowed with physical beauty, strength, and wealth;
for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, they shall not encounter eons of pestilence.
At last one meets the King of Dharma Physicians, Who forever uproots the source of birth and death.
By constructing latrines to remove the filth of the masses, One later suffers no more from the affliction of excrement.
Body and mind are perpetually pure; All who see them cannot help but rejoice.
By virtue of this, one leaves all defilements behind and ultimately attains great peace.
If one practices giving for the sake of being born in the heavens, or seeks fame and reputation,
or to repay a kindness, or out of a desire for reward, or out of fear—
The fruits obtained will not be pure, and what one receives will be largely coarse and harsh.
If ancestors established acts of giving and descendants continue them without interruption,
those born into such a lineage will enjoy the inherited blessings of immeasurable wealth and treasures.
One who constantly praises the merit of giving, yet possesses wealth but does not relinquish it,
will always be born into poverty and destitution, wishing to give but having no material goods.
One who constantly praises the virtue of generosity and always pities others with universal compassion—
Those who attain great wealth in their rebirths yet constantly delight in cultivating wisdom but do not practice giving,
will be born ever intelligent and wise, yet remain poor and destitute of property.
If one delights solely in practicing generosity but does not cultivate wisdom,
one will obtain great wealth in future births, yet remain ignorant and devoid of insight.
If one cultivates both generosity and wisdom, one will be endowed with both wealth and knowledge in future births.
Those who cultivate neither of these two will dwell for a long night in poverty and darkness.
Lacking right faith in giving, though they later obtain abundant wealth,
all that they receive will be coarse and harsh, and their minds will always delight in attachment.
With deep faith, one practices giving and bestows gifts;
One is born with superior wealth and treasures, And all that is received is adorned, The mind always filled with love and joy.
Knowing well the excellent field of merit, One offers with reverence and gladness.
The kinsmen one gives birth to will be harmonious, and all shall together receive the retribution of peace and happiness.
If one’s mind is always disdainful toward giving and offers to the fields of merit with an arrogant intent, one will have great wealth in future lives;
yet though one obtains it, one will be unable to use it.
Those of inferior character have no extraordinary learning and are not respected or admired by the multitude.
If one does not disparage the practice of giving, but instead reverently cultivates merit and wisdom,
one will obtain superior wealth upon birth, and one's kinsmen will all honor and respect them.
Bestowing gifts as is appropriate, his mind is always joyful;
he obtains wealth according to his wishes and enjoys it through the Path.
Gaining possessions by means of principle, he practices giving with wisdom.
Wealth and treasures arrive spontaneously; whatever is obtained is never lost.
Giving at the proper time meets with no obstacles; one who understands clearly cultivates merit and wisdom.
Seeking little, one gains much; one always obtains what is appropriate for the occasion.
If a person cultivates pure conduct, they will distance themselves from what others cherish and obtain a virtuous wife at birth, fully endowed with beauty and grace.
The wise always avoid improper places and improper times for action.
With a peaceful mind and free from transgression, Fully possessing the qualities of a great man,
Cultivating the pure holy life praised by the noble ones,
One’s body remains ever fresh and clean, And one’s renown spreads far and wide.
Beheld with reverence by all people, And honored by all the devas—
If a person in this world Stays far from wine and leaves behind delusion,
Possessing a firm will free from error, They shall attain the peerless eloquence of meaning.
If a person does not speak falsely, being sincere and free from deception,
they will receive a body complete in all its parts and will not be stained by an evil reputation.
If a person does not engage in divisive speech, using skillful means to harmonize disputes, they will attain a body with well-proportioned limbs.
Born as the most honored among humans, one’s retinue shall never be broken.
If a person refrains from harsh speech, using beautiful words that please the listeners,
they will constantly hear pure sounds and proclaim the supreme, wondrous Dharma.
If a person in this world avoids meaningless speech,
speaking with sincerity and at the proper time, knowing the right measure and speaking what is beneficial,
their words will always be correct in future lives, and those who hear them will joyfully follow their practice with faith.
If one does not covet the property of others, And never gives rise to thoughts of seeking it,
The mind that arises will be peaceful and joyful, And one will always obtain superior,
celestial wealth. If one does not give rise to anger, Nor the intent to strike, bind, or oppress others,
Always delighting in the cultivation of loving-kindness and patience, one will later be reborn ascending to the Brahma Heaven.
If, in this present life, a person possesses deep faith and perfect view,
speaks truthfully regarding existence and non-existence, and associates with virtuous friends—
Later born as a God among Gods, with the light of wisdom surpassing that of the sun and moon;
as has been proclaimed above, through immeasurable pure deeds,
one receives various worldly retributions according to one's conduct.
If you desire great benefit, renown, or the joy of rebirth in heaven,
and seek permanence within impermanence, you should diligently cultivate the roots of virtue.
By performing pure and impure deeds, one adorns various fruits [of karma].
If one is born among human beings, one receives a mixture of black and white retributions.
Whether as a child, in the prime of youth, in middle age, or in old age,
each experiences the retribution of suffering or joy according to their respective original conditions, alternating between them.
When various karmas have been performed and increase, one receives their results in succession;
though performed, if they do not increase, the retribution is obtained only after a long time.
If a person’s giving is not constant, it will lead to poverty and destitution in the interim.
If one constantly practices giving, wealth and joy will be inexhaustible.
If a person harbors much anger, they will always be ugly in future births;
if one is compassionate, patient, and free from wrath, they will receive a body that is always upright and handsome.
If a person does not cultivate wisdom, the delusion that arises will be dark and obscure;
one who prizes knowledge and practices much hearing becomes clear-sighted and meets with the worthy and holy.
If one can subdue arrogance, they will be reborn into a superior lineage.
Foolish and deluded, yet self-important and haughty, they are always born among the lowly and base.
Through flattery and sycophancy their bodies become crooked; with deceitful speech they appear short and ugly.
Seeing the Sages, their hearts feel no joy; thus, wherever they are born, they remain ignorant and dull-witted.
Mute and unable to speak, blind and seeing nothing;
though one speaks with a compassionate heart to console them, they reject it with indifference and refuse to listen—
such a person shall be born deaf and dumb.
By offering exquisite incense and flowers, the person who is thus reborn will possess a physical form that is entirely dignified and majestic; their body will be exceedingly supple and pure,
like refined, genuine gold.
Committing sexual misconduct in improper places, harming physical forms and destroying sentient beings—
due to these, one receives a eunuch’s body.
When the mind of lust blazes intensely, so too do the body, speech, and all the sense faculties.
Having fully mastered the ways of women, she later constantly took female form;
though possessing great desire and lacking wisdom,
she expounded the path of purity and showed the correct road to those who were lost.
Regarding all sentient beings with equal love, one later attains the pure eye,
clear and unobstructed.
Out of compassion for the poor and the sick, one gives birth to many descendants.
Like the moon among the stars,
one who observes the fast and cultivates pure conduct, cherishing that which is loved by others,
shall not violate anything at all.
Born with many beautiful women surrounding him for his own enjoyment,
like Śakra, Lord of the Devas;
revering all those worthy of honor, he will be perpetually noble in future lives.
The body is exceedingly supple;
firmly maintaining the practice of the Vinaya, one later attains immovable wealth,
like the King of Snowy Mountains.
Always not transgressing the rules of propriety, whether others ask or do not ask,
one gives equally until they are satisfied; in a future life,
one will obtain the excellent mark of a lion-like jaw and possess inexhaustible wealth.
Like an island of rare jewels in the ocean, he practices generosity as well; free from envy toward others, he does not guard his own wealth.
By the retribution of such karmic actions, [he attains this state].
One will be reborn later in Uttarakuru.
If a person seeks fame and reputation, or desires the pleasures of rebirth in heaven,
they should rely upon a virtuous teacher for study, keeping body, speech, and mind pure.
All manner of wealth and possessions, One cherishes and guards with great care;
By reason of such karmic conditions, One is later reborn into a royal household.
If in this present life, one is resolute in will and does not follow others,
Their conduct is full of illusion and deceit, yet they also cultivate various wholesome dharmas;
they take pleasure in watching the quarrels and disputes of others while simultaneously practicing the giving of alms.
Due to the causal conditions of these karmic actions, they later become asuras.
Through filial piety and pure offerings to parents and all elders,
through patience and little anger, and by not delighting in viewing strife or litigation—
by virtue of these karmic conditions, one is reborn later in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
If a person does not fight themselves, nor observes the quarrels of others,
but diligently cultivates wholesome dharmas, they shall attain birth in the Yāma Heaven.
By observing the body well, delighting in study, and accumulating great learning, one attains this state.
Diligently contemplating the meaning and delighting in cultivating pure merit,
through the causal conditions of these deeds, he was later reborn in Tuṣita Heaven.
Having practiced sublime generosity and delighted in reciting the various sūtras, he attained this state.
Practicing wholesome dharmas through skillful means, by one's own power and not depending on others,
and through diligent perseverance, one will later be reborn in the Heaven of Delighting in Transformations (*Nirmāṇarati*).
Cultivating superior generosity and properly restraining and protecting the sense faculties,
Diligent and never turning back, Rejoicing in the virtues of others—
Through the causal conditions of these deeds, One is later reborn in the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Emanations.
Having abandoned the burning fires of desire, One cultivates the four sublime abodes.
Free from applied and sustained thought, accompanied by joy born of seclusion, one is reborn in the Brahma palace. Furthermore,
with a mind free from both applied and sustained thought, having transcended even the joy born of seclusion,
accompanied by the joy and bliss born of concentration, one is reborn above in the Ābhāsvara Heaven.
Free from the joy and pleasure born of concentration, dwelling entirely in the company of bliss,
with equanimity, mindfulness, and samādhi, they are reborn in the Heaven of Universal Purity.
Having completely transcended both suffering and pleasure, they dwell in a state that is neither painful nor pleasant.
Through equanimity and pure mindfulness, one is born in the Heaven of Vast Fruit (Bṛhatphala).
By perceiving the transcendence of thought and becoming weary of the five kinds of existence,
yet deeply craving non-conceptualization, one is born in that Heaven of Non-conceptualization (Āsaṃjñika).
Through mundane and untainted cultivation of various permeated dhyānas,
by the power of the correct reception of these permeated dhyānas, one is born in the five Pure Abodes.
By cultivating the soft and medium grades, one is born in the Heaven Free from Affliction (Avṛha) and the Heaven Free from Heat (Atapa).
By cultivating the three superior grades, one is subsequently reborn in the three Pure Heavens.
Following this sequence upward, one reaches even the Akaniṣṭha Heaven.
Relying on the perception of the impermanence of form, one transcends to cultivate the immeasurable sphere of space.
Next, one contemplates immeasurable consciousness, Abandoning it until reaching nothingness;
Then departing from nothingness, One proceeds even to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
I have already explained birth and death, Along with their various fruits and retributions.
Regarding those karmic fruits and retributions, the wise should investigate them.
One should cultivate pure karma; thus one leaves suffering behind and swiftly attains happiness.
Having already explained the various distinctions of karma throughout all births and deaths.
Not born from the creation of Īśvara, nor existing spontaneously,
not produced by time nor without cause, it arises solely from afflictions.
Observing that existence is impermanent, the wise do not become stained by attachment.
Having emerged from all fetters, one reaches the state of eternal peace.
The Brief Sūtra on the Analysis of Karmic Retribution.
